argument:
TSMC's latest issuer quarter reports NT$1,270.38bn revenue and NT$706.56bn net income, a derived net margin of 55.62%. This substantial realised profitability gives the foundry bull case an operating foundation rather than solely a semiconductor-demand forecast. The board-approved NT$7 per-share dividend is observed distribution evidence; broad technology spending makes continued capacity utilisation a plausible upside scenario.

No incremental growth surprise follows merely from board approval, and current debt/FCF and overseas-fab economics need review. Taiwan concentration and capital intensity remain material risks. ADR EPS of US$4.31 must not be confused with ordinary-share EPS. Strong moving-average and MACD trends support interest, but RSI near 88 without strong volume makes new-entry timing demanding.
key_points: Observed earnings and high derived margin support the operating foundation.
Dividend approval is evidence of distribution, not a growth surprise.
Geographic, capex and technical-extension risks limit entry conviction.
